title: SLO-driven shortfall simulation and buffer targets for hosted endpoints
content:
Purpose:
This working doc captures simulation-driven scenarios to quantify SLO-aligned headroom for Redwood's Hosted API. Goal: produce per-region tokens/sec and QPS buffer targets that keep p95 latency under 150ms and error rate <0.2% across modeled surges, while minimizing reserved GPU overhead. This is an operational working sheet (draft) intended for review by infra, SRE, and serving-runtime teams before formalizing capacity commits.

Summary of approach (short):
- Use recent 90-day traffic histograms (token length, seq-length distribution, user burstiness) to drive Monte Carlo surge simulations.
- Apply model mix (chat-heavy vs. embeddings-heavy) per customer segment to estimate per-request token cost.
- Convert token demand to GPU-seconds using profiling matrix per GPU family + model variant.
- Map GPU-seconds to required device count under continuous-batching latency SLO constraints.
- Derive deterministic headroom (reserve) targets per region to cover N-minute incident windows, regional failover traffic, and correlated multi-customer spikes.

Key assumptions used in sims:
- Baseline median request size: 170 tokens (prompt + response), 95th percentile: 620 tokens.
- Model mix for Hosted: 60% chat/generation (decoder models), 30% instruction/condense, 10% embeddings.
- Typical tokens/sec per GPU (baseline mix): A100-80GB = 650 t/s, H100-80GB = 980 t/s, L4-48GB = 220 t/s (these are effective throughput under our continuous-batching runtime with preferred quantization profiles).
- Target latency SLO: p95 <= 150ms for short responses (<=256 tokens); for long responses (>256 tokens) target p95 <= 400ms.
- Outage or throttling windows considered: 5m, 15m, 60m.
- Confidence targets: size headroom to meet SLOs with 99th percentile of simulated surges for 15-minute windows.

Simulation scenarios (representative):
1) Localized microburst (10x short-lived spikes): 10x baseline QPS sustained for 90s concentrated in one AZ, then back to baseline.
   - Outcome: latency climbs but KV-prefix cache avoids regen cost for 70% of repeated tokens.
   - Recommended reserve: +25% tokens/sec buffer in that AZ (prewarm pool of smaller L4 slices + ability to burst to H100 when latency crosses 125ms p95).

2) Regional sustained surge (3x for 20 minutes): multi-customer marketing event driving 3x sustained QPS for 20m across the region.
   - Outcome: without reserve, p95 breaches 150ms in ~7m due to backpressure in batching queues and cache pressure.
   - Recommended reserve: +40% tokens/sec regional buffer (mix: keep 60% on dedicated H100 pool, 40% as elastic A100 reserved that can be shared across regions via warm standby).

3) Correlated cross-region spike (2x in primary + failover from another region): primary region doubles and takes additional ~0.5x traffic from failing region for ~15m.
   - Outcome: global routing throttles at 0.9x threshold unless regional pre-allocations exist; cascading fallback caused momentary 2.2x load in specific model variants.
   - Recommended reserve: inter-region surge policy with auto-fallback routing enabled and +30% global buffer distributed across secondary regions.

Representative numeric outputs (from Monte Carlo run #42):
- North America (prod-us-central): baseline 1,800K tokens/sec (aggregate), peak 15m 5x observed in sample => simulated 9,000K t/s. 99th percentile surge coverage requires 2,600K t/s additional headroom.
- Europe (eu-west): baseline 600K t/s, 99th percentile shortfall ~900K t/s.
- APAC (ap-southeast): baseline 220K t/s, but higher variance; reserve target is conservative +200% for short 5–15m microbursts.

Table — recommended per-region buffer targets (plain text table):
Region | Baseline t/s | 99p surge t/s | Recommended reserve (t/s) | Reserve as % of baseline | Reserve GPU equiv (H100)
US-CENTRAL | 1,800,000 | 9,000,000 | 2,600,000 | 144% | 2,650
EU-WEST | 600,000 | 2,000,000 | 900,000 | 150% | 920
APAC-SG | 220,000 | 660,000 | 440,000 | 200% | 450
Notes: GPU equiv computed using H100 effective 980 t/s. We recommend a mixed strategy (some H100 reserved, some A100 burstable) rather than pure H100 reservation due to cost/elasticity tradeoffs.

Operational levers and their simulated impact:
- Continuous batching tuning: increasing batch aggregation window by 25ms reduces required GPUs by ~12% but increases p95 by ~8ms. Tradeoff acceptable for background workloads, not for low-latency chat routes.
- KV prefix cache warm ratio: improving warm cache hit from 60% to 80% reduces short-lived microburst cost by ~18%.
- Model quantization: moving non-sensitive generation to q4_0 profiles yields ~30% t/s uplift on A100 but requires careful eval on quality.
- Smart routing: sending lower-priority customers to A100-only pools during surges preserves H100 capacity for high-SLO customers, simulated p95 improvements of ~20% for priority tokens.

Headroom policy proposal (operational):
- Per region maintain two bands: Operational Reserve (OR) for common surges: 30–60% of baseline depending on variance; Critical Reserve (CR) for high-confidence 99p events: separate pool equal to simulated shortfall for 15m window (numbers above).
- OR should be filled with cheaper, faster-to-scale instances (A100 or L4 depending on region); CR should be H100-backed or in dedicated capacity to avoid noisy-neighbor risk.
- Maintain a global warm-standby pool equal to 20% of total OR across regions to handle correlated cross-region spikes.

Routing & throttling triggers (runbook-ready):
- Trigger A (preemptive scaling): if p95 latency > 110ms for two consecutive 1-minute intervals AND queue length > 80% capacity -> spawn +10% A100 pool and shift low-priority customers.
- Trigger B (failover): if any region experiences 5xx error rate > 0.2% for 3 minutes -> route 20% of traffic to nearest secondary region and enable degraded-cache mode (longer TTLs for prefixes).
- Trigger C (emergency throttling): if aggregate token burn rate > CR capacity + OR and p95 > 200ms -> circuit-break 5% of trial/credit-tier traffic and escalate to oncall.

Cost implications (order of magnitude):
- Holding CR in H100-heavy reserved capacity increases monthly committed spend by ~28% in high-volume regions but reduces expected SLO-violation incident cost by estimated $XXk/month (modeled as support + revenue risk). Final numbers require finance input.

Open questions & action items:
- Re-run Monte Carlo with updated model-mix from product (expected shift to more short-turn chat for Q1 2028). Owner: Lina. Deadline: 2028-01-20.
- Evaluate quality impact of q4_0 quantization on our top-10 customer prompts. Owner: Ethan. Deadline: 2028-01-31.
- Define exact carve-outs for priority-tier routing in Router service; create routing policy PR. Owner: Marcus. Deadline: 2028-02-07.

Appendix: quick simulation knobs (for reproducibility)
- Seed: 2027-11-01-rng42 
- Traffic model source: aggregated s3://infra-metrics/hosted-api/traffic-hist-90d.parquet
- Profiling matrix: infra/profiles/gpu_throughput_matrix_v3.csv
- Monte Carlo config: 10k iterations, mixture-model sampling, correlated-customer bursts enabled

End of working draft.
Feedback welcome — please add review comments inline in Drive or drop notes in #infra-capacity.
